records.title: Killing cells by targeting mitosis.

administered_agents.name: microtubule poisons (class named, individual agents not given in the saved string)
administered_agents.role: review mention of clinically used agents

records.model: not applicable (review of antimitotic therapeutic strategies in cancer)
records.note: Reviews strategies for killing cancer cells by targeting mitosis: microtubule poisons with proven clinical efficacy, inhibition of CDKs, Aurora and Polo kinases and spindle motors, and explicitly notes that abrogating the mitotic checkpoint, or targeting the energetic or proteotoxic stress of aneuploid or chromosomally unstable cells, may add benefit by inducing lethal levels of instability, while inhibiting APC/C to block mitotic exit generates metaphase cells that invariably die in mitosis. Efficacy of cell-cycle-targeting approaches has so far been limited.
records.uncertainty: A review with no primary data and no named agents (house rule 7), written entirely from the perspective of killing cells. Its value to this project is as counter-evidence rather than candidacy: it states plainly that checkpoint abrogation and selective energetic or proteotoxic stress are the recognised ways to kill aneuploid and checkpoint-compromised cells, which is a direct safety constraint on the appraised energy-stress (metformin/AICAR), proteasome-blockade and APC/C-directed entries in a child whose tissue mass may depend on aneuploid cells. It provides no amount, no BUBR1 data and no non-malignant tissue evidence.
records.source_abstract_quality: review abstract with agent names and some clauses dropped; upstream_completeness_not_verified

records.title: Mps1 regulates spindle morphology through MCRS1 to promote chromosome alignment.
records.model: human cells; Mps1 and MCRS1 manipulation with spindle and alignment assays
records.note: Beyond recruiting checkpoint effectors to unattached kinetochores, the SAC kinase Mps1 binds and phosphorylates the spindle assembly factor MCRS1 to control the dynamics of the minus end of kinetochore fibres and enable KIF2A localisation there, thereby actively promoting chromosome alignment.
records.uncertainty: Mechanism from genetic manipulation with no compound administered, no BUBR1 measurement, no in vivo work and no muscle endpoint. Its practical value is as a constraint: Mps1 (TTK) has a separate, pro-alignment function, so pharmacological Mps1 inhibition of the kind appraised under reversine and CFI402257 would be expected to degrade alignment as well as checkpoint signalling in a cell that is already segregation-compromised.
records.source_abstract_quality: abstract with the spindle assembly factor named only once and several clauses dropped; upstream_completeness_not_verified

records.title: Bub1 mediates cell death in response to chromosome missegregation and acts to suppress spontaneous tumorigenesis.
records.model: allelic series of mutant mice with graded Bub1 protein reduction: Bub1 hypomorphic (strong reduction) versus Bub1 haploinsufficient (milder reduction) versus wild-type
records.note: A protein-dose experiment on a checkpoint component: both hypomorphic and haploinsufficient mice have weakened checkpoint activity and elevated aneuploidy, and both have similar chromosome missegregation rates, yet cell death after an aberrant division falls sharply as Bub1 declines, and only the hypomorphs (below a critical threshold) are highly susceptible to spontaneous tumours while the haploinsufficient mice are not. But it is the cleanest statement in this slice that checkpoint-protein abundance behaves as a threshold variable for tumour risk rather than a linear one, which is the premise the restoration route rests on, and it locates the danger in the cell-death arm rather than in the missegregation rate.

It is relevant background for the ledger's DEVD-CHO entry on caspase-dependent BUBR1 degradation, and it carries an explicit caution - caspase-2 is tumour-suppressive and protects against genomic instability - so broad caspase inhibition in a cancer-predisposed child cuts both ways. records.title: Multiple mechanisms determine the order of APC/C substrate degradation in mitosis.
records.model: Living budding yeast cells with GFP-tagged APC/C-Cdc20 substrates, quantitative fluorescence microscopy
records.note: APC/C-Cdc20 substrate destruction is ordered by several distinct mechanisms: Clb5 degradation begins early in mitosis, followed 6 minutes later by securin and Dbf4, and anaphase begins when less than half of securin is degraded. The spindle assembly checkpoint delays Clb5 but not securin degradation; early Clb5 degradation needs Cdk1-Cks1 binding and an ABBA motif, while securin and Dbf4 are delayed by Cdk1 phosphorylation near their Cdc20-binding sites.
records.uncertainty: Budding yeast with no drug (house rule 2 does not apply, but no compound exists here at all). Directly relevant to interpreting substrate-level readouts - it shows the SAC does not delay all APC/C substrates equally and that anaphase starts with securin only partly degraded, which is a concrete reason why preserved securin or cyclin levels cannot be read as checkpoint status (house rule 4). It provides no candidate, no mammalian data and no muscle endpoint.
records.source_abstract_quality: One substrate name dropped from the first sentence ('ordered degradation of and other proteins'); results otherwise complete.

records.title: A role for the mitotic proteins Bub3 and BuGZ in transcriptional regulation of catalase-3 expression.
records.model: Neurospora crassa (filamentous fungus) with Bub3 deletion and BuGZ mutants including GLEBS-domain and zinc-finger mutations
records.note: The spindle-checkpoint proteins Bub3 and BuGZ negatively regulate catalase-3 transcription in Neurospora. Loss of Bub3 significantly decreased BuGZ protein levels; Bub3 and BuGZ interact directly via the GLEBS domain, but it is BuGZ protein amount rather than the Bub3-BuGZ interaction that sets cat-3 expression. BuGZ binds cat-3 chromatin and blocks recruitment of GCN4/CPC1 and NC2, preventing transcriptional assembly.
records.uncertainty: Fungal genetics with no compound (house rule 2). One detail is conceptually adjacent to this patient: losing one GLEBS-domain partner lowers the other partner's protein level, and BUBR1 binds Bub3 through its own GLEBS domain - so partner abundance may be coupled. But this is Neurospora, the readout is catalase transcription rather than mitotic fidelity, no BUBR1 is involved and no drug exists here; it cannot support or constrain any candidate.

records.title: The EGF/hnRNP Q1 axis is involved in tumorigenesis via the regulation of cell cycle-related genes.

administered_agents.name: epidermal growth factor (EGF)
administered_agents.role: administered stimulus in vitro, endogenous growth factor

records.model: Colorectal cancer cell lines with hnRNP Q1 level manipulation and EGF stimulation; human colorectal cancer tissues; RIP-seq
records.note: hnRNP Q1 binds a set of mitotic mRNAs and raises Aurora-A protein without changing its mRNA, i.e. by translational control; EGF stimulation increases both hnRNP Q1 binding to Aurora-A mRNA and the efficiency of that translation, and the effect is mediated by the mTOR and ERK pathways. hnRNP Q1 also upregulates translation of a group of spindle assembly checkpoint genes, and its overexpression correlates with Aurora-A and SAC gene levels in human colorectal cancer tissue.
records.uncertainty: This is a translational-control route to raising spindle-assembly-checkpoint protein abundance - the same axis as this project's restoration route, which currently works through NAD/SIRT2-mediated BUBR1 stabilisation rather than synthesis - and it carries a specific constraint the ledger does not: the abstract places mTOR upstream of that translation, so mTOR inhibition would be expected to lower, not raise, SAC protein output. That bears directly on the demoted everolimus and sirolimus entries and argues they should stay demoted on this patient's protein-supply lesion. Heavy caveats: the SAC genes are not individually named, so BUBR1 itself is not shown to be among them; the manipulation is expression-level plus a growth-factor stimulus, not a drug (house rules 2 and 7); the system is colorectal cancer cells, where the same axis is presented as tumorigenic, making upregulation dangerous in a child with recorded rhabdomyosarcoma; and there is no muscle, fidelity or in vivo endpoint.
records.source_abstract_quality: Several clause fragments dropped ('genes that are involved in mitotic including Aurora-A'); the identities of the 'group of spindle assembly checkpoint genes' are not given in the saved string.

records.title: Proliferation of Double-Strand Break-Resistant Polyploid Cells Requires Drosophila FANCD2.
records.model: Drosophila hindgut papillar cells, a naturally polyploid tissue with impaired DNA damage responses; in vivo organ development
records.note: Polyploid Drosophila papillar cells accumulate broken acentric chromosomes yet neither apoptose nor arrest, and continue dividing with normal organ development; surviving mitosis with acentric chromosomes requires the Fanconi anemia proteins FANCD2 and a partner plus Blm, but not canonical DNA-damage-response signalling. FANCD2 acts independently of prior S phase to promote alignment and segregation of broken DNA, avoiding micronuclei and organ defects.
records.uncertainty: Drosophila genetics with no compound at any point (house rule 2). It is nonetheless the closest record in this slice to the project's central tension - how a tissue keeps developing normally while dividing with damaged or unbalanced genomes - and it identifies a specific tolerance machinery that prevents micronuclei rather than killing the affected cells. But it is an invertebrate polyploid tissue, not aneuploidy, not BUBR1, not mammalian muscle, and the authors themselves frame the tolerance mechanism as cancer-promoting.
records.source_abstract_quality: The second Fanconi protein's name is dropped ('FANCD2 and as well as Blm'); findings otherwise legible.

The authors propose Mis6 acts as a platform for Mad2 accumulation.
records.uncertainty: Yeast genetics with no compound. Checkpoint-protein recruitment mechanism only; no BUBR1, no abundance restoration, no mammalian, fidelity-outcome or muscle data.

records.title: Multi-kinase inhibitors can associate with heat shock proteins through their NH2-termini by which they suppress chaperone function.

administered_agents.name: AR-12 (OSU-03012)
administered_agents.role: administered drug; GRP78 chaperone inhibitor used as proteomic bait and as treatment

administered_agents.name: sildenafil
administered_agents.role: administered drug in combination with AR-12

records.model: Tumour cell lines of multiple genetic backgrounds; proteomics with AR-12 as bait, in situ immunofluorescence with domain-specific antibodies, SDS-PAGE and western blotting, in silico docking, and GRP78/HSP27 overexpression rescue.
records.note: AR-12 associates with multiple ATP-binding chaperones through their NH2-termini, reduced their detection by N-terminal but not central or C-terminal antibodies while total protein on western blot was unchanged, dispersed their punctate subcellular patterning, inhibited chaperone ATPase activity and blocked chaperone-chaperone and chaperone-client interactions. Combined with sildenafil it activated an eIF2a/ATF4/CHOP/Beclin1 pathway, inactivated mTOR and raised ATG13 phosphorylation, producing toxic autophagic puncta; overexpressing GRP78 and HSP27 prevented the ER stress activation, preserved mTOR activity, blocked MCL-1 downregulation and preserved tumour cell viability. The authors conclude that chaperone inhibition very likely explains the antitumour effects of AR-12 and of multi-kinase inhibitors across genetically diverse tumour cells.
records.uncertainty: Recorded as a harm-direction constraint, not a candidate. This patient's restoration route depends on the opposite move, propping up a destabilised missense BUBR1 protein, which is why the ledger carries chaperone-supporting entries such as arimoclomol and teprenone alongside HSP90 inhibition; a record showing that multi-kinase inhibitors as a class suppress chaperone function is a reason to look hard at the chaperone consequences of any kinase inhibitor considered for this child. The claim about multi-kinase inhibitors generally is the authors' inference rather than a tested panel in the saved string, the work is entirely in tumour cell lines with no normal or muscle tissue, no in vivo arm, no BUBR1 measurement, and the rescue arm is overexpression, not a drug.
